"But now let's be focused on (the next race) Austin. The performance this weekend was OK. We have to be focused on the future."
Hamilton's blunder means his lead over fourth-placed Max Verstappen in the drivers' standings has been cut to eight points, following the Dutchman's maiden Singapore Grand Prix victory.--AFP
d98c4f181d4c235a: THE 2027 Budget 2027 carries a headline figure of RM510 billion.
For a household deciding whether it can afford the month's groceries, school expenses and loan repayments, the more consequential figure is what remains in its bank account.
That is the distance this budget must bridge: between national economic performance and personal financial security.

The budget offers meaningful relief within constrained public finances. Its central challenge is to turn a modest increase in federal spending into a sustained improvement in household purchasing power.
Reconciling growth, household protection and stronger public finances deserves recognition. Yet allocations express intentions. Their value will be established through implementation.
Beyond the RM510 Billion Headline

The first requirement is clarity about the numbers. The RM510 billion envelope includes federal expenditure alongside investment by government-linked investment companies, public-private arrangements, statutory bodies and MoF Incorporated companies.
Their financing and implications for public finances differ. The rise from RM470 billion to RM510 billion, about 8.5 per cent, compares the broader announced envelopes.
Direct federal expenditure, meanwhile, increases from the revised RM444.1 billion estimate for 2026 to RM459.8 billion in 2027: about
RM15.7 billion, or 3.5 per cent. Development expenditure rises from RM81 billion to RM83 billion.
These are different comparisons. The federal increase is nominal, before changing costs, and does not by itself establish the net fiscal stimulus.
Composition and execution will determine the result. Assistance can support consumption quickly. Education, healthcare and infrastructure can raise productive capacity over many years.
Procurement delays and poorly chosen projects can diminish both effects.

Local supplier networks are equally important. Investment generates wider benefits when Malaysian firms provide components, services and expertise, and workers acquire skills that support higher earnings.
Imported technology can raise productivity substantially; the policy task is to develop the skills and supplier capabilities that allow more of its benefits to remain in Malaysia.
Investment in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing and the energy transition must build domestic capacity alongside attracting capital.
Regional development belongs within the same framework. Stronger Penang-Kedah manufacturing connections and better integration of Sabah and Sarawak's production economies can spread opportunity.
Reliable utilities, logistics and supplier development should connect smaller firms and less-developed regions to expanding markets.
The Household Balance Sheet

The announced minimum-wage increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 from June 2027, subject to exemptions for qualifying MSMEs, and the increase in individual income-tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000 give substance to the household-income agenda.
The reach of these measures requires attention. Workers employed by firms qualifying for the exemption cannot assume that the new wage floor will apply to them.
Smaller employers need practical support to improve productivity and sustain higher pay, with progress assessed through workers' earnings.
Tax relief also needs precise explanation.
An additional RM3,000 deduction reduces taxable income; it does not provide RM3,000 in cash.
The benefit depends on the taxpayer's circumstances. Households without income-tax liability receive no direct gain from that deduction.
Combined STR and SARA allocations rise from RM15 billion to RM16 billion. Timely assistance matters greatly to families with little financial buffer.

Targeting must, however, reflect how people live. Identical household incomes can support very different living standards depending on the number of dependants, disability, medical needs and location.
Eligibility records need regular updating, accessible appeals and sensible arrangements for households whose incomes fluctuate.
For middle-income families, the deeper difficulty is the cumulative cost of housing, food, commuting, childcare, healthcare and debt.
Occasional relief helps, but these recurring obligations require sustained policy attention.
Affordable homes must be connected to employment. Public transport must be dependable enough to reduce reliance on private vehicles.
Healthcare and childcare must be accessible enough to lower unavoidable expenses and enable people to work.
These services are part of household economic security. Their quality determines how much private spending families must undertake. A wage increase goes further when essential services work well.
Fiscal Discipline Must Earn Its Keep
The fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of GDP, against 3.6 per cent in 2026, is achievable, but conditional.
The 2026 estimate has already been revised from 3.5 per cent following pressure on fuel subsidies.
The Finance Ministry's published baseline projects a modest decline in the deficit from about RM78.5 billion to RM77.5 billion. Growth in the economy contributes materially to the improved ratio.
There is underlying adjustment too: the primary deficit, which excludes interest payments, is projected to fall from 1.0 to 0.7 per cent of GDP.
However, the tables explicitly exclude new 2027 Budget measures. The cost and financing of those measures must therefore be reconciled with the baseline before the full fiscal impact can be assessed.
Weaker growth would affect revenue; expensive energy could increase subsidy costs.
Higher petroleum receipts need not match the timing or scale of that expenditure. Debt servicing, projected at approximately RM61 billion, will absorb about one ringgit in six of federal revenue.

This constrains choices even where the case for investment is strong. Published estimates put revenue at RM380.8 billion against operating expenditure of RM376.8 billion, leaving just RM4 billion before development spending. This narrow margin strengthens the case for sustainable revenue reform.
Better compliance and a review of ineffective tax concessions can broaden the base while distributing the burden more fairly.
Household tax relief should be assessed alongside the lasting revenue needed for dependable healthcare, education and infrastructure.
Building on e-Invoicing and existing reforms, the government should explain what additional revenue will finance and how vulnerable households will be protected.
Public confidence depends on seeing taxes translated into services that work. Operating expenditure should nonetheless be judged fairly.
Teachers, nurses, medicines and maintenance are indispensable to development. A hospital building without sufficient staff and equipment cannot deliver the expected public benefit.
The task is to improve value across the budget: complete useful projects, maintain assets, strengthen procurement competition and discontinue weak programmes.
Public-private partnerships can supplement investment, provided future government payments, guarantees and user charges are transparent.
Fiscal discipline earns its keep when it limits the future interest burden and preserves resources for services, investment and emergencies.
Delaying essential projects or payments merely to improve an annual ratio would undermine that purpose.
Over the coming year, progress should be measured through wages after inflation, employment quality, household savings, investment actually undertaken and service delivery.
These outcomes must be examined across states and income groups, with external conditions considered alongside the budget's contribution.
The 2027 Budget has set a constructive direction. Malaysians should be able to recognise its results in better work, dependable services and greater capacity to save.
That is how growth earns public confidence: by making ordinary life more secure.

677cca15a40cbc82: NEW YORK: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani said that the city would investigate the Immigration and Customs Enforcement shooting that left a man wounded on Thursday.
Mamdani told MS NOW on Sunday that he and New York City Police Department officials would “review the entire 24-hour period.”

The investigation will include the ICE shooting, the police response and ensuing protests, and ICE’s use of a privately owned parking lot as a staging area, Mamdani said. It will also address what steps the city can take “to make New Yorkers safe.”

Mamdani said late Thursday he had urged president Donald Trump to halt all ICE enforcement actions in the city after spending two hours on the telephone with the president and department of homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin in an unsuccessful effort to secure the man’s release. He said on MS NOW that he told Trump and Mullin that ICE operations were “making the city less safe.”
New York governor Kathy Hochul said she had also spoken with Trump and Mullin, urging them to halt operations and release body-camera footage.
Mullin said Sunday he would “absolutely” release the body camera footage after the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations conclude their reviews.

Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican man, was shot during what the homeland security described as a targeted operation in the Marble Hill neighbourhood. Mullin maintained on Fox News Sunday that Belgal was accelerating the vehicle as ICE officers were approaching.

At least seven rounds were fired, hitting Belgal in the neck, according to Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch. He was treated at a hospital, and the 5-year-old child in his vehicle was physically unharmed.
Marcos Charles, who leads ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations, said agents used their vehicles to block Belgal on Thursday afternoon and that he refused orders to get out of his car.

The NYPD on Friday released body camera footage of the aftermath of the shooting, showing Belgal handcuffed behind his back and suffering from a gunshot wound to the neck as officers arrived. An ICE agent wearing gloves applied pressure to the wound while an officer called for an ambulance.
Rather than wait, officers carried Belgal by his arms and legs to a police vehicle to drive him to the hospital.

Charles said Belgal had a criminal record in New York that included charges of robbery, grand larceny and theft while armed with a deadly weapon. The department of homeland security said Thursday that he was in the US illegally and had ties to the Trinitarios gang, without providing further details.
A federal judge on Friday barred his deportation, and he was taken Friday afternoon to the Metropolitan Detention Center, a federal jail in Brooklyn, a government lawyer told a court.
a095bd96422c15fc: KUALA LUMPUR: Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP) has facilitated RM123.81 billion in financing approvals for Malaysian businesses since 2009, reflecting continued demand for funding support among enterprises.
As at Aug 31 this year, the cumulative approvals under its current government guarantee schemes involved 148,795 accounts and 90,503 borrowers.
For the January-August 2026 period, SJPP approved RM7.46 billion in financing involving 10,240 accounts.
SJPP principal officer Juanita Rusmini Abdul Jalil said the schemes were designed to facilitate access to financing for eligible businesses through participating financial institutions (FIs).

"These figures indicate continued financing demand among Malaysian businesses. SJPP's role is to administer government guarantee allocations and work with participating financial institutions to facilitate access to financing," she said.
The financing can support working capital, capital expenditure and business expansion.

Under the Government Guarantee Scheme Madani 2026 (GGSM4), eligible businesses can access facilities ranging from term loans and revolving credit to hire purchase, trade financing and bank guarantees, subject to scheme conditions and lenders' assessments.
Eligible small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can obtain financing of up to RM20 million per company under GGSM4, while eligible mid-tier companies can access up to RM30 million.
"The inclusion of eligible mid-tier companies recognises that financing requirements can become larger and more complex as businesses scale up," Juanita said.

GGSM4 makes RM30 billion available across economic sectors, with targeted focus areas covering Bumiputera businesses, halal, tourism, high-growth high-value sectors and export-oriented mid-tier companies.
Wholesale and retail trade, restaurants and hotels accounted for 44.8 per cent of cumulative sector-based financing approvals as at Aug 31.
This was followed by manufacturing, including agro-based activities, at 17.1 per cent.
Construction contributed 13.2 per cent, while finance, insurance, real estate and business activities accounted for 12.3 per cent.
Together, the four sectors represented about 87 per cent of approvals by sector.

SJPP is also streamlining guarantee processing through its Self-Approved Arrangement (SAA), which allows participating FIs to process eligible guarantee applications within predetermined limits and parameters.
In August, SJPP approved 1,798 applications, its second-highest monthly number for the year up to that point.
Financing approvals reached RM1.35 billion, the highest monthly amount recorded from January to August.
About 64 per cent of August approvals were processed through SAA, with an average processing time of one working day.
"Speed and efficiency matter when businesses need financing for working capital or investment.
"Our processes aim to shorten the processing journey for eligible applications while maintaining governance and eligibility requirements," Juanita said.
She added that financing approvals were only one measure of impact, with the broader objective being to help eligible businesses sustain operations, invest and grow.
Verified post-financing data and beneficiary case studies could provide a clearer picture of the schemes' outcomes.

7526f88ee05ccdfe: KUALA LUMPUR: Higher emoluments, retirement charges and debt servicing are driving government operating expenditure 3.8 per cent higher to RM376.8 billion in 2027.
This is despite the expected fall in subsidies and social assistance in the 2027 Budget, according to Kenanga Research.
Emoluments, the largest component of operating expenditure, are forecast to increase 2.9 per cent to RM111.6 billion next year from RM108.4 billion in 2026.
This will account for 29.6 per cent of the government's total operating spending, Kenanga Research noted.
The firm attributed the increase to annual salary increments and additional healthcare and education staff, including those required for the two-cohort Year One intake.
Retirement charges are expected to climb 4.2 per cent to RM44.6 billion as the number of pensioners and beneficiaries grows.
The government is also moving towards a defined contribution scheme to manage long-term pension liabilities.
Debt service charges are projected to increase 6.5 per cent to RM61 billion, representing 16.2 per cent of operating expenditure. Domestic debt accounts for 98.4 per cent of the total.
Meanwhile, subsidies and social assistance are forecast to fall 2.3 per cent to RM72.7 billion from RM74.5 billion in 2026.
But it will remain the second-largest operating expenditure component, accounting for 19.3 per cent of the total.
Kenanga Research said the decline reflects continued subsidy rationalisation through BUDI95, Budi Diesel and the nationwide Electronic Cooking Oil Subsidy System.
However, spending is expected to remain elevated following upward revisions to the 2026 subsidy requirements amid higher energy prices.
The projected reduction therefore reflects gradual efficiency gains rather than a significant withdrawal of government support.

Kenanga Research said with the Finance Ministry assuming Brent crude oil prices of US$85 per barrel, effective subsidy targeting and tighter controls on leakage will remain crucial to containing fiscal pressures while safeguarding eligible households.
f23750c0294ac548: In my previous column, I wrote about LIDAC26, the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference hosted by cryptocurrency exchange Luno in Kuala Lumpur on Sept 24, and confessed that my favourite session had nothing to do with regulators or stablecoins.
It was a breakout on Malaysian builders shaping the global digital asset landscape, and I haven't been able to stop thinking about it since.

Here's why. Talking to participants and reading reports, I found that if you have ever checked the price of a coin, traced a transaction on Ethereum or swapped one token for another on Solana (two of the world's busiest blockchains), there is a decent chance you used something that started in Malaysia, whether you knew it or not.

That's not just national pride talking: Tiger Research, a crypto research firm, said as much in its 2025 report on our market: "Etherscan, Jupiter, Virtuals Protocol, and CoinGecko all started in Malaysia and now have global reach."
The crypto world's price list

Start with CoinGecko, which Bobby Ong, an economics graduate of University College London, and TM Lee, who studied computer science at Purdue University, founded in Kuala Lumpur in April 2014. It began by tracking a mere 20 coins and now covers more than 21,000 crypto assets across over 1,000 exchanges, drawing what it says are more than 10 million users a month.
What I find most remarkable is how they got there, with no venture capital and no first hire until January 2018.

"Choosing not raising venture capital allowed us the opportunity to not need to relocate to Silicon Valley, one of the most expensive locations to live in," Ong told CryptoSlate in 2021, while Lee put it even more bluntly to The Edge: "There were no parents to bankroll us. We kept it low-cost and kept reinvesting; this helped us stay in the game."

In January, CoinDesk reported that CoinGecko was weighing a sale at a valuation of around RM2 billion. Not bad for a startup whose founders, The Edge reported in 2021, worked remotely before renting their first office in Taman Tun Dr Ismail.
The window into Ethereum
Then there is Etherscan, launched in 2015 by Matthew Tan. Think of it as a search engine for the Ethereum blockchain: punch in a wallet or transaction and it shows you exactly where the money went.

Back in 2019, The Edge reported that Tan was running the business out of Shah Alam with a team of just 15, and that it was already profitable. Since then, Etherscan says it has ranked among the world's top 1,000 websites by traffic, and in 2024 it bought Solscan, a popular explorer for the rival Solana blockchain.

Today, a team of more than 70 runs over 60 explorers, and developers can pull data from more than 50 blockchains with a single Etherscan key. That's right, the explorer Tan built and launched back in 2015 now reaches across much of the crypto world.
Solana's best-price finder

Next up is Jupiter, co-founded by Siong Ong, who sat on that LIDAC panel. Jupiter is an aggregator, which means it scans Solana's many trading venues for the best price and then makes the swap for you, even splitting your order across several venues if that gets you a better deal.

The numbers are staggering: according to data tracker DefiLlama, Jupiter has routed more than RM5 trillion in trades to date, and handled almost RM60 billion in the past 30 days alone, about half of all aggregator volume on Solana.
When Jupiter launched its JUP token in January 2024, it handed out a billion tokens to more than a million wallets, and it has since grown into perpetual futures, lending and a mobile wallet.
And the bench runs deep

Virtuals Protocol, co-founded by Jansen Teng, lets anyone launch and co-own artificial intelligence (AI) agents. Its token briefly topped a market value of RM20 billion in January 2025, and in February this year it launched Eastworld Labs to put humanoid robots to work, because, in Teng's words, they "are currently hamstrung by two fundamental bottlenecks: lack of data and capital".

Virtuals said more than 18,000 AI agents had already been deployed on its platform, alongside a fleet of more than 30 full-sized humanoid robots. Being in the robotics industry myself, I can tell you that is no small feat.

Then there is Pendle, a marketplace that lets investors trade the future yield on their crypto, a little like stripping a bond's coupons from its principal and selling them separately. Binance Labs, then the venture arm of the world's largest crypto exchange, backed it in 2023, and at its peak in September 2025 it held more than RM54 billion in deposits.
Tiger Research counts Pendle among the global projects in which "Malaysian talents also play key roles".

Sure, crypto is volatile, and several of these figures sit well below their peaks today. But the point is not the price of any single token; it is that a country of our size keeps producing the people who build tools much of the industry relies on.

Sitting in that breakout room two weeks ago, it struck me that the three founders on stage had, between them, built the price list, the search engine and the best-price finder that millions of crypto users lean on every day, and that all three companies started right here in Malaysia.
It's about time we celebrated them like the world-class builders they are.

095f495008cc648a: KOTA BHARU: When Nik Imanuddin Hadeef Nik Izdiharuddin was tasked with a Year Two science assignment, neither he nor his mother imagined where it would lead.
Two years later, the 10-year-old is learning to manipulate wayang kulit puppets, practising different character voices and playing the traditional instruments that accompany performances.
He can also draw and carve his own puppets, and has already made his first appearance before an audience.
“I want to be a doctor, but I also want to play wayang kulit until I die,” Imanuddin told Bernama at his home in Kampung Kubang Sipot here.

His mother, Nur Hazween Hasni, was the one who came up with the idea. “His teacher wanted them to create an object that could produce a shadow. So, I suggested we make wayang kulit puppets," the 39-year-old recalled.
Using cardboard, they crafted characters including Dewa Panah and Pohon Beringin for Imanuddin to take to school. That exercise quickly developed into something much bigger.
“After I submitted the assignment, I went home and asked my mother to make more puppets, one after another,” the boy recalled.
Among his favourites is Pak Dogol from “Hikayat Seri Rama”, whom he admires for being able to battle jinn and other powerful creatures.

He has since become more comfortable moving the puppet behind the screen while adjusting his voice and intonation to suit different scenes. The voices, however, remain one of the hardest parts to master.
“Every character has its own voice, which is part of its identity, and the puppeteer has to make sure the audience can distinguish each character just by its voice,” he said.
“For me, it is really difficult to switch from one voice to another.”
Finding a mentor on TikTok
His curiosity eventually took him to TikTok, where he discovered videos by Kelantan wayang kulit practitioner Kang Boon Ann, better known as Che Ann.
“I was scrolling through TikTok when I came across Che Ann’s page. Since then, I have followed his posts. I also wanted to meet him,” he said.
That meeting finally happened early last year, and Imanuddin was accepted for training with Che Ann’s Sri Cindayu Wayang Kulit Association.
Under his mentor’s guidance, he has been learning puppet manipulation, traditional music and the basics of becoming a tok dalang.
His training also led to his first public performance in Tok Bali early last year. “I was very happy because it was my first time performing in front of people,” Imanuddin expressed.
Being onstage required more than the practice he was accustomed to at home. He had to manage his nerves, keep his movements precise and stay focused throughout the performance.
Although it remains his only public appearance so far, he hopes there will be more opportunities ahead.
Nur Hazween says wayang kulit is one of several artistic interests her son has picked up. He already enjoys drawing and playing instruments such as the recorder and keyboard.
“He really likes the arts. He enjoys drawing and music too. But when I saw how deeply he was getting into wayang kulit, I realised that his interest lies more in traditional arts,” she said.
She believes some of that inclination may come from her father, Hasni Mat Hassan, 74, a former arts lecturer at the Institute of Teacher Education. Drawing also runs in the family.

More striking to her has been the change in her son since he began performing and training regularly. "He used to be shy, but now he is more confident. His interaction with people has also improved, including when he performs."
That confidence has spilled into other areas of school life, including storytelling and Da’i Cilik competitions, where he has had more opportunities to speak before an audience.
Nur Hazween nevertheless makes sure wayang kulit does not interfere with his studies. Practice and training sessions are arranged around his school schedule.
“We must not allow this traditional art to be forgotten with time. We have to pass it on to the next generation so that they know about it and do not forget it,” she added.
43983ad5167e72e4: Saya tanya Google makna spoiled brat dalam bahasa Melayu. Jawapannya ‘budak manja’. Apa pula makna brat? Kata Google ‘anak nakal’. Saya simpulkan spoiled brat bermakna ‘budak manja yang nakal’? Atau mungkin juga ‘jahat’ instead of sekadar ‘nakal’?
Definisi Inggeris begini: A spoiled brat is a child or perhaps a person who acts badly, throws tantrums or shows no regards for others because they are used to getting whatever they want.
Bagi saya itulah dilakukan Donald Trump setiap kali tidak dapat apa yang beliau mahu. Maklum anak orang kaya. Cuma Trump bukan seorang budak. He is 80 years old and president of the United States.

His latest tantrum ‘meletup’ beberapa Jumaat lalu apabila beliau tidak dianugerahkan the Nobel Peace Prize 2026. Tentu kita ingat tahun lalu pun beliau tidak dapat anugerah itu meskipun ‘beriya-iya’ mahukan kemenangan.

Pemenang 2025 ialah Maria Corina Machado, pemimpin pembangkang Venezuela. Machado ialah musuh politik Nicolas Maduro yang semasa menjadi presiden Venezuela telah ‘diculik’ Trump dan dibawa ke AS untuk menghadapi the US justice system berhubung tuduhan jenayah berkaitan dadah.
Machado menyerahkan pingat emas Nobel Peace Prize yang dimenangi kepada Trump sambil mengucap terima kasih kepada presiden AS itu mengambil tindakan ke atas Maduro dan rejimnya.

Pemenang Nobel Peace tahun ini tidak tunjuk tanda akan mengikut langkah Machado. Malah, Navanethem atau Navi Pillay semasa dimaklumkan mengenai penganugerahan itu memberitahu kawan-kawanya yang bertepuk tangan menyambut berita gembira itu if you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump. Sinis.
Navi Pillay, peguam hak asasi kemanusiaan dari Afrika Selatan pernah membela Nelson Mandela ketika pemimpin terkenal itu melawan dasar aparteid Pretoria.

Sebaik saja penganugerahan Navi diumumkan, Trump merungut, memberontak dan mengamuk persis spoiled brat. Navi diperkecilkannya. “The Nobel prize was given out to a liberal person who works at the United Nation who nobody has ever heard of,” kata Trump.

Sebenarnya, Navi is not somebody nobody has ever heard of. Navi dikenali ramai sebagai ketua hak asasi manusia PBB yang mempengerusikan suruhanjaya yang merumuskan Israel bersalah melakukan genosid di Gaza.

Jadi, tidaklah memeranjatkan Benjamin Netanyahu mengkritik keras penganugerahan Navi. Oleh kerana Trump sahabat baik Netanyahu dan merestui apa dilakukan Israel di Gaza beliau senada dengan pemimpin Israel itu.
Tetapi, yang membuat Trump berapi tidak diberi Nobel Peace Prize adalah beliau melihat dirinya seorang pemimpin yang menghentikan perang .

“The United States of America represented by me as your president should have received the Nobel Peace Prize but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision.

"The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical idealogues who are anti democracy and really enemies of civilization. We will not forget Norway that you didn’t give this prize.”
Trump menjadikan Norway sasaran kerana Nobel Peace Prize dianugerahkan oleh jawatankuasa negara itu.

Trump mendakwa beliau telah selesaikan lapan peperangan. Kata CNN ini tidak betul. Yang menarik ialah peringatan Daniel Dale menerusi analisisnya juga di CNN bahawa Trump started an ongoing war with Iran. Benar. Tanpa peringatan Dale pun kita tentu ingat Trump bersama Netanyahu memulakan perang ke atas Iran pada 28 Feb lalu. Sehingga sekarang perang berterusan, dan Trump terus mengancam mahu menghapuskan Iran .

Selain pernah menjadi pesuruhjaya PBB mengenai hak asasi manusia, Navi Pillay juga pernah menjadi hakim Mahkamah Jenayah Antarabangsa dan pernah memegang jawatan presiden tribunal jenayah antarabangsa mengenai Rwanda dan sekarang memegang jawatan itu untuk tribunal mengenai Myanmar.

Saya tidak pasti sama ada kedudukan dan peranan Navi dalam Mahkamah Jenayah Antarabangsa atau ICC ada kena-mengena dengan tindakan pentadibran Trump mahu membubar atau “dismantle the ICC brick by brick,” kata Setiausaha Negara Marco Rubio.
Kata Rubio, AS akan mengenakan pelbagai sekatan termasuk cutting off the court’s resources to stop investigations into US personnel and allies like Israel.

Jelas AS tidak mahu ICC bertindak katas Tel Aviv meskipun Israel melakukan genosid di Gaza. Dan bagi, Mahkamah Jenayah Antarabangsa ‘tidak ada hak mengambil tindakan terhadap warganya’. Ertinya walaupun jika mereka melakukan jenayah antarabangsa.
Pada masa lalu ICC mengambil beberapa keputusan yang tidak disenangi AS dan Israel. ICC pernah keluarkan waran tangkap ke atas Netanyahu dan bekas menteri pertahanannya Yoav Gallant.

Setiausaha Agung PBB, Antonio Guterres menyifatkan keputusan pentadbiran Trump yang diumumkan pada hari Navi diisytihar pemenang Nobel Peace Prize 2026 a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice of which the ICC is a key pillar.
United Kingdom bersama Kanada, Denmark, Jerman, Perancis, Itali, Jepun dan Belanda menzahirkan rasa kesal terhadap tindakan AS dan strongly disagree with the sanctions.
Lapan negara itu menegaskan sokongan tidak berbelah bahagi dan berterusan terhadap ICC.
ICC adalah institusi kehakiman penting dalam membawa keadilan kepada mangsa jenayah antarabangsa. Sesungguhnya ia mesti dipertahankan. ‘Persetankan’ keputusan Trump.

ce7d0486bb363733: ADDIS ABABA: Sekurang-kurangnya 139 migran maut, manakala 84 lagi hilang selepas sebuah bot membawa 350 orang terbalik di perairan Djibouti, menurut Pertubuhan Antarabangsa untuk Migrasi (IOM) pada Ahad, lapor Xinhua.

Bot itu dalam perjalanan dari Djibouti ke Yaman apabila terbalik pada malam antara Khamis dan Jumaat. Menurut agensi Pertubuhan Bangsa-bangsa Bersatu (PBB) itu, pasukan IOM berada di lokasi bersama pihak berkuasa tempatan bagi memberikan bantuan kecemasan.

"Ini merupakan kehilangan nyawa amat menyedihkan. Simpati kami kepada mangsa terselamat serta keluarga yang kehilangan orang tersayang atau masih menanti khabar ahli keluarga mereka," kata Ketua Misi IOM di Djibouti, Alexandre Coissac.
"Tragedi ini menjadi peringatan jelas bahaya yang dihadapi migran di sepanjang laluan migrasi ini ketika mereka mencari peluang ekonomi."
Agensi migrasi PBB itu dalam kenyataan pada Ahad memaklumkan daripada 109 mayat yang ditemui, 52 ialah lelaki, 42 wanita dan 15 kanak-kanak.

Lebih 80 orang terselamat dalam nahas bot itu dan semuanya warga Ethiopia, manakala pihak berkuasa Djibouti meneruskan operasi mencari dan menyelamat di tengah-tengah kebimbangan terhadap mereka yang masih hilang.
Pihak berkuasa tempatan turut memberikan rawatan perubatan kepada mangsa terselamat serta menguruskan pengebumian secara terhormat bagi mangsa korban.
Nahas bot terbaharu itu antara beberapa tragedi seumpamanya yang meragut banyak nyawa di kawasan pesisir Laut Merah Djibouti.

1808cc68687caceb: PARIS: Eurodeputy Raphael Glucksmann was on Sunday elected the centre-left candidate for next year's French presidential elections, organisers of the vote said, winning comfortably in the first round.
Glucksmann, 46, who leads the centre-left Place Publique party, won 66% of the 120,787 votes cast in the primary.
Socialist Party leader Olivier Faure was a distant second with 14% of the vote, and the other three candidates scored less than 10%.
"This result says something powerful," Glucksmann posted on X. "A left that is faithful to its values can unite, govern and win."
Glucksmann presents himself as a break from the policies of French President Emmanuel Macron and one who can beat the far right.
But he is currently polling at between nine and 14%, well behind the frontrunner, far-right candidate Marine Le Pen.
He also trails centre-right contender Edouard Philippe, who served as prime minister under Macron, and hard-left veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon, whose France Unbowed party boycotted the primary.
When in August he announced his intention to run for the presidency, he distanced himself from what he called "classical political" circles.
Instead, he emphasised his past work abroad, in the aftermath of genocide in Rwanda and as a former adviser to the anti-Moscow former Georgian president Mikheil Saakashvili.
Elected to the European Parliament in 2019, Gluckmann's work there has also focused on human rights and he has been a staunch defender of Ukraine.
While Glucksmann strikes a more reformist and centrist tone than the Socialist Party, he has cooperated with them in the past, presenting joint electoral lists.
And now, it is in his interest to work with the venerable party and benefit from its campaign machine.
But he has ruled out any cooperation with Melenchon, still the leading contender on the left.
His critics say he is "too Parisian", too detached from the realities of everyday French people to be a credible candidate.
In response, he underlines his past human rights work in conflict zones such as Rwanda.
"My outlook and my view of the world were not forged in Davos or Washington, but in places whose desolation I'm not sure you can even begin to fathom," he has said.
During his campaigning across France this summer, he put forward a programme rooted in the left that tries to reconcile ecological transition with social progress.
The first round of France's presidential election is set to take place on Sunday, April 18, with the second round set two weeks later on May 2.

536b5e554a8de23c: PANAMA CITY: Panama has recorded more than 200 aftershocks following Friday's 7.7-magnitude earthquake that damaged hundreds of homes and infrastructure across the country's central provinces, prompting the government to declare a national state of emergency over the weekend.

No deaths have been reported, but at least 27 people were injured and nearly 900 homes have been damaged, according to emergency authorities, though the figure could rise as assessments continue in remote communities.
The emergency declaration will allow the government to allocate up to US$100 million in relief funds without exceeding its 2026 fiscal deficit target of 3.5% of GDP, the economy ministry said.

"We have already recorded more than 200 aftershocks, and they are continuing, but their magnitude is decreasing and the intervals between them are getting longer," Nestor Luke, director of the University of Panama's Institute of Geosciences, told Reuters.
The US has pledged US$5 million in assistance and is sending a 20-member team to help with rescue operations and infrastructure assessments, US Ambassador Kevin Marino Cabrera said.

President Jose Raul Mulino visited affected areas to deliver aid and called for urgent repairs to roads and bridges to facilitate relief efforts. At least 14 bridges were damaged in the provinces of Veraguas and Los Santos.
Classes were suspended nationwide on Monday, while the Panama Canal said shipping operations remained unaffected by the earthquake.
f72514834e9282e7: LONDON: Manchester City gave a defiant response after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules as the leaders romped to victory at Liverpool.
Manchester United's miserable start has put boss Michael Carrick under pressure, while Bruno Guimaraes came to Arsenal's rescue.
AFP Sport looks at three talking points from this weekend's action:
Man City win exacerbates uncertainty

In any other season, Manchester City would be in pole position in the title race after a flawless start that includes statement wins away to their two biggest rivals in Liverpool and Manchester United.

Yet, whether Enzo Maresca's men are in the running for the title at all is clouded in uncertainty until a ruling on their appeal against a guilty verdict on more than 100 charges of breaking financial rules.

City managed to shut out the noise surrounding their trip to Anfield, powering to a 3-0 win thanks to goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki after Liverpool were reduced to 10 men by Ryan Gravenberch's red card.

Yet, the sight of City sitting top of the table with a perfect record from their opening six games will only intensity the calls for a swift resolution to the case to prevent the issue hanging over the world's most watched league.
Man Utd hit 40-year low point
Manchester United's return of six points from their opening six league games is the club's worst for 40 years as they again failed to take advantage of playing against 10 men.
Tottenham rallied from being both a goal and a man down to level through Dominic Solanke in stoppage time at Old Trafford and a 1-1 draw was the very least the visitors deserved.

Only poor finishing cost Tottenham a first league win of the season after they bossed United for long periods to put more scrutiny on Michael Carrick, just months after he was handed the United job on a permanent basis.
United lost 1-0 to Manchester City last month despite playing for over an hour with a man advantage and did likewise in losing at home to Everton last season.
Carrick now faces a crucial 10 days with tough away games at Atletico Madrid, Leeds and Como.
"The pressure is on him, the questions are obviously always with the manager and you just hope they can come out of it in these next few weeks," former United captain Gary Neville said.
Arsenal's Guimaraes makes his point
Bruno Guimaraes stated his case to start for the Premier League champions after the Brazil midfielder came off the bench to seal Arsenal's 2-1 win against Leeds.
Arsenal were in danger of a second successive defeat when they fell behind at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday.
But after Riccardo Calafiori's equaliser, former Newcastle star Guimaraes landed the decisive blow just minutes after he was introduced as a second-half substitute by Gunners boss Mikel Arteta.
It was Guimaraes' second league goal since his close-season move to north London and his first at the Emirates.
Guimaraes hopes his contribution can guarantee a start in Arsenal's Champions League home game against Lille on Tuesday.

"I felt amazing and I can't wait to score more goals now. It was very loud when I scored. I want to hug them (the Arsenal supporters) for everything they have been doing for me," Guimaraes said after diving into the crowd in celebration of his goal.
Guimaraes has made just one league start for second-placed Arsenal and Arteta said he "wasn't at the level" required during that loss at Brighton.
"I couldn't wait to go to the pitch and I was very anxious on the bench. So, getting in the game and scoring an important goal is always a very good feeling," Guimaraes said.
4248ff1494aeee2f: PETALING JAYA: A RM7.1 billion federal budget allocation for defence and security equipment should be used to solve years of underinvestment in the armed forces, a defence analyst says.

Izzah Khairina Ibrahim of the Institute of Strategic and International Studies Malaysia said that defence spending had been kept at about 1% of the country's GDP, despite equipment having exceeded their service life.
She said military assets might not be adequate against threats ranging from non-traditional security challenges, grey-zone coercion, asymmetric, hybrid threats and high-tech warfare.

"Despite gradual progress, modernisation remains slow, with development expenditure accounting for only 34% of the total allocation this year, compared to the 65.7% for operational expenditure," she told FMT.
The 2027 budget allocates RM22 billion each to the defence ministry and the home ministry, a 1.2% increase from the 2026 allocations.

The large allocations to the defence and home ministries reflected a cautious and pragmatic approach to national security, as Malaysia recognised that security and public order could not be maintained by military means alone, she said.

However, sustained investment was needed in civilian and military territorial domain awareness, defence cyber and electromagnetic capabilities, and secure, integrated communication and coordination systems.
Lam Choong Wah of Universiti Malaya said the armed forces needed the funds for major modernisation plans, including those of the navy and air force.

Lam said the defence ministry should receive more than the home ministry because of the costs of operations and procurement,; however, with the government’s main focus on easing the cost of living, other sectors such as defence would have to give way.

Mizan Aslam, a senior fellow at the Global Peace Institute, welcomed the rise in the defence ministry’s allocation over the past five years. The increase was needed, given territorial claims in the South China Sea and tensions in the Middle East.
"We need more assets and a system that can accommodate the changes in our world right now," he said.
86c42fc21c2ad724: From Khairul Hafezad Abdullah
When a heavy-rain warning appears on our phones, most of us understand what it means. We know which roads usually flood, which rivers may rise, and which neighbourhoods have been affected before.
Yet knowing that a risk exists is not the same as being prepared for it.

After a major flood, we often hear people say: “We never thought it would get this bad.” Often the problem is not always that we failed to see the danger. We saw it, understood it - and carried on as usual.

This is a familiar challenge in safety management. When people are repeatedly exposed to a hazard without serious consequences, their perception of risk can change. What once caused concern begins to feel normal.

Consider a family in a flood-prone area. The water may have reached the front gate several times but never entered the house. This past experience becomes reassurance: “It happens every year. The water will subside."
But the next flood does not have to behave like the last one. A hazard does not become less dangerous simply because we are accustomed to it.

Malaysia today has far better access to information than it did decades ago. Weather warnings reach our phones quickly, while river levels, road closures and evacuation centres can be monitored almost in real time.

The real question is what we do with that information. Do we move vehicles to higher ground, secure important documents and medicines, check on vulnerable family members or neighbours, and know where to go if evacuation becomes necessary? Or do we read the warning, glance outside, and continue as usual?

According to the statistics department, floods caused an estimated RM636.9 million in losses nationwide in 2025. Public assets and infrastructure accounted for RM380.2 million, while damage to living quarters amounted to RM183.8 million.
But preparedness should begin before we start counting losses.
Imagine being told you have 10 minutes to leave your house. What would you take? Who would need assistance? Where would you go? Would everyone know what to do?
For households with elderly people, young children, persons with disabilities or family members requiring regular medication, these questions matter even more.
Communities matter, too. In the first moments of an emergency, rescue personnel cannot be at every doorstep. Sometimes, the first person able to help is a neighbour.
A prepared community knows which households may need assistance, which roads become inaccessible first, and how reliable information can be shared quickly.

From an occupational safety viewpoint, good safety management does not wait for someone to be injured before action is taken. Hazards are identified, risks assessed and reasonable controls are introduced beforehand.
Why should disaster preparedness be any different?

Preparedness does not mean living in constant fear, nor does every warning require panic. It means accepting risk and uncertainty as part of the package, and taking reasonable action before circumstances become critical.
So when the next warning appears on our phones, perhaps the question should not be: “Will it really get that bad?” It should be: “If it does, are we ready to act?”
Khairul Hafezad Abdullah is a senior lecturer in occupational safety and health management, and a reader of FMT.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

Felo kanan di Global Peace Institute, Mizan Aslam mengalu-alukan peningkatan peruntukan kepada Kementerian Pertahanan sejak lima tahun lalu. Peningkatan itu diperlukan memandangkan isu pertikaian wilayah di Laut China Selatan dan ketegangan di Timur Tengah.

f1424f9136002ea0: RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s main airport came under renewed attack from Houthi rebels, a day after a strike on the facility killed 12 people and heaped pressure on the Middle East’s biggest economy as it prepares to host major events that seek to boost foreign investment.

An unidentified projectile hit a passenger terminal at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Sunday, with authorities tackling a blaze, the Saudi-led coalition that’s fighting Iranian-backed Houthi militants in Yemen, said in a statement. The Houthis swiftly claimed the attacks, saying they were a response to “Saudi aggression,” including a strike on the airport in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa.
The Saudi civil aviation authority said that the attack killed one person and injured 11. The coalition also said air defences had intercepted a missile near the same location in the Saudi capital.

A projectile also fell near the King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia’s Dammam, which the Houthis also claimed as one of their attacks.

The blast at the Riyadh airport on Saturday brought travel at the airport to a near-standstill. It also forced the capital’s financial hub to shift to remote work until further notice and prompted executives from BP Plc and Shell Plc to pull out of a major energy event in the city this week.

The Federal Aviation Administration on Sunday issued a warning to all US airlines to exercise caution flying to or over parts of Saudi Arabia “at all altitudes”.

Authorities have indicated the 25th World Petroleum Congress and associated events, due to run from Sunday through Oct 15, will go ahead. The city is also scheduled to host the Future Investment Initiative, Riyadh’s flagship investor gathering, later this month.

Saturday’s strike came less than a week after Saudi-backed forces in Yemen launched a campaign to retake Houthi-held areas and “eliminate” the group. The rebels, who frequently claim attacks on Saudi oil facilities, had recently seized more Yemeni territory and bolstered their control over the Bab el-Mandeb, a global shipping choke-point.
The Saudi-led coalition called “the cowardly terrorist attack” on the airport on Saturday “a full-fledged war crime” by the Houthis.
The victims included four Saudis, a Palestinian, two Bangladeshis and one person each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Sudan, according to authorities.

6d0ed66c1a30ea1a: ABU DHABI: Manchester City's problems are easily explained in Abu Dhabi, home of the scandalised team's royal owners, where fans agree: they're victims of a Premier League conspiracy.
Across the oil-rich city, supporters believe there's more to City's woes than meets the eye, saying English football's traditional powers are employing dark arts to neutralise an upstart rival.

"Of course," replied Obeid Al-Heifeiti, 22, without hesitation, when asked if other clubs played a role in the seismic verdict that City broke Premier League financial rules more than 100 times from 2009 to 2018. The club has lodged an appeal.
"I think that's part of it, if a club is successful," said his friend Salman Al-Otaiba, 29, on Sunday, as they watched City dismantle Liverpool 3-0 at a sports bar on Saadiyat island.

The same view was repeated across Abu Dhabi, the UAE's well-heeled, skyscraper-studded capital and centre of its oil wealth. Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United are ganging up on City, supporters say.
"It's exaggerated," said an Emirati father at a busy mall on Yas Island, referring to the case against City, flanked by his son wearing the team's replica shirt.
"All these famous clubs, they're doing something in the background," added the bespectacled father, who asked to remain anonymous. "It does not need to be on this level."
A short drive away in a dusty, suburban strip mall, Khalil Al-Khodri was shopping in ManCity Tailor, which specialises in kandooras - the distinctive white robes worn by many Emirati men.
"Behind the scenes there's always someone who's benefiting," he said.
"It's not a Man City issue. It's someone who would like to create chaos so he gets something. It's quite obvious they want to take advantage of this situation right now."
'They're out to get us'

The Emirati owners took over Manchester City in September 2008, not long after oil hit an all-time record of US$147 per barrel. The Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, was still under construction in Dubai.

It was a period of global outreach as the wealthy nation, founded just 37 years earlier, turned its attentions to international assets and soft-power projects, holding its first F1 grand prix in Abu Dhabi in 2009.
City, after decades in the doldrums, secured their first Premier League title in unforgettable fashion in 2012, with Sergio Aguero's injury-time winner against QPR in the last game of the season.

Seven more English league titles have followed, six during manager Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden reign, when they also bagged their first treble - the Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League - in 2022-2023.
The Emirati owners will now feel "slighted" by the independent commission's ruling, and may believe "they're out to get us for political reasons", a Gulf football writer and broadcaster told AFP.
"They (owners) believe that this is some of the more traditional members of the Premier League protecting their own clubs against outsiders," he said, requesting anonymity.
"They don't believe they've done anything wrong."
He added: "There's a lot of pride in what they did with the team with Pep Guardiola, the trophies they won and the quality of the team.
"There's also a lot of cultural pride. It's a part of the world where honour and pride are very important in dealing with business - a person's word, a person's honour is very important."
'Booze has run out'
Billionaire royal Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, UAE vice-president and deputy prime minister, is not the only Gulf Arab behind a major European club.
Qatari ex-tennis player Nasser al-Khelaifi is president of Paris Saint-Germain, the reigning European champions who paid a still-record transfer fee of €222 million for Brazil's Neymar in 2017.
Saudi Arabia's oil-funded Public Investment Fund snapped up England's Newcastle United in 2021. However, tighter financial rules have frustrated expectations that the club would spend big on players.
"There certainly was a lot of displeasure in Saudi Arabia when it comes to Newcastle, that they weren't allowed to spend certain amounts of money," the Gulf football expert said.
"It seemed that the minute they bought Newcastle, the rules changed to make it harder and harder to invest in the club and players.
"Newcastle are coming to the party after the booze has run out."
